label: before and after: pahle and baad
note: pahle and ke baad are introduced by HI-C90-pahle and HI-C90-baad. The note read in full 'Nothing can be sequenced in time', and that was true: the track could state facts about a day and not put two of them in an order, so a one-minute prepared description was four unrelated statements. The pair is asymmetric and the lessons say so rather than inventing a reason -- before takes se (X se pahle) and after takes ke (X ke baad) -- and ke baad is shown to be the possessive ka/ke/ki already taught for uska and hamara, used as glue: the after OF work.
